verdict.summary: You can create an app and install it in your own workspace in minutes, and Activate Public Distribution needs no review. Commercial distribution effectively needs a Marketplace listing, which requires 10 active installs and a multi-week review.
verdict.hands_on_effort: 1-2 hours for gates 1-2; 2-5 days for a Marketplace submission
verdict.approval_wait: None for own workspace and unlisted installs; Marketplace review is up to 10 business days preliminary plus up to 10 weeks functional

gates.name: Development workspace install
gates.unlocks: Create the app and install it in the one workspace that owns it.
limits: A new app can only be installed in its own workspace by default

gates.name: Unlisted public distribution
gates.unlocks: Other workspaces can install via the Add to Slack button or a shareable install URL.
limits: Workspace owners can restrict installs to Marketplace apps
Admins can require approval before members install
Commercial unlisted apps created after May 29, 2025 get conversations.history/replies capped at 1 request/min and 15 objects per request
Slack positions unlisted distribution for pilots and testing
Tokens do not expire unless you opt into rotation
gates.time_to_reach: About 30 min after the checklist is done

gates.name: Slack Marketplace listing
gates.unlocks: Commercial distribution, removal of the conversations.history cap, and install in workspaces that allow only Marketplace apps.
limits: Needs at least 10 active-workspace installs for the whole review
Scopes that trigger enhanced review slow the process
After publishing, the live version is locked and changes need re-review
gates.time_to_reach: Weeks to months, including getting 10 active installs first

steps.title: Decide: managed Composio auth or your own Slack app
steps.detail: Managed auth works for your own workspace or a private pilot. Register your own app if you want a trimmed scope set, to distribute to other workspaces, or to list in the Marketplace.

steps.title: Create the Slack app
steps.detail: Sign in at api.slack.com/apps and create a new app, either from scratch or from a manifest. Your client ID and secret are on the App Management page.

steps.title: Set the redirect URL
steps.detail: In the app's OAuth settings, add the Redirect URL. It must use HTTPS and have no fragment. Create the Composio auth config first so you can copy the callback URL from it.

values.label: Redirect URI
values.value: Composio callback URL (see the Composio callout on this page)

gotchas: With several redirect URLs registered, the same redirect_uri must be sent in both the authorize and token calls, or Slack returns bad_redirect_uri

steps.title: Choose a minimal scope set
steps.detail: Pick scopes from the API methods you actually call. Prefer bot tokens and use user scopes only when a specific user must act. Avoid the *:history, search:read.*, and files:read scopes unless you have a clear need. Slack's Marketplace rules disqualify admin.*, identity.*, and search:read.
gotchas: Scopes cannot be removed from an existing token without revoking it
Existing installs must re-authorize to receive added scopes

steps.title: Add credentials to Composio and connect your account
steps.detail: Enter the client ID and secret in your Composio Slack auth config, then install the app to your workspace and run a test authorization. Check that the state value is verified and that you exchange the code within ten minutes.

steps.title: Prepare the app for other workspaces
steps.detail: Serve all OAuth redirect, interactivity, options load, and Events API URLs over SSL, using TLS 1.2 or higher. Then open Manage Distribution and complete every checklist item.

steps.title: Activate Public Distribution
steps.detail: Click Activate Public Distribution in Manage Distribution. This unlocks the Add to Slack button and a shareable install URL. One community source says it needs no review and takes effect at once.
gotchas: Workspaces limited to Marketplace apps will block you, and approval-mode workspaces need an admin decision

steps.title: Get 10 active installs
steps.detail: Marketplace submission is blocked until the app is installed in at least 10 active workspaces, meaning used in the last 28 days and not sandboxes. Keep the count at 10 or more through the whole review.

steps.title: Prepare listing, policy, and review materials
steps.detail: Draft a public landing page with no login, an Add to Slack path, a privacy policy, a support page, and a written justification for every scope. Make 1600x1000 images and a 30-90 second demo video. The privacy policy must give an email or web form for contact.
gotchas: Do not request scopes for features you have not built

steps.title: Test end to end on a non-development workspace
steps.detail: Test install, use, and uninstall on a workspace that is not your development workspace. Give reviewers a way to install the app and test credentials for any connected service, because they cannot use your Slack workspaces.

steps.title: Submit for Marketplace review
steps.detail: Submit from the app's App Management page. Automated checks run first, then a preliminary review (up to 10 business days), then a functional test (up to 10 weeks for new apps).

steps.title: Wait for review and respond to feedback
steps.detail: Slack will not speed up review to match a launch date. Resubmitting during the preliminary stage resets your queue place. Once a reviewer has the app in the functional stage, resubmitting keeps your place.

requirements.item: HTTPS redirect URL registered in App Management
requirements.detail: No fragment; must match or sit under a registered Redirect URL.

requirements.item: SSL on all app URLs and TLS 1.2+
requirements.detail: Covers OAuth redirect, interaction, options load, and Events API URLs.
Required from July 2026 and for the whole review.

requirements.item: Public landing page, privacy policy, support
requirements.detail: Support must reply within 2 business days; the privacy policy needs an email or web form.

requirements.item: Production-ready app tested on a non-dev workspace, with demo video
requirements.detail: Reviewers need an install path and third-party test credentials.

Listed as disqualifying for Marketplace apps.

scopes.scope: search:read.* (public, private, im, mpim, files, users)

scopes.effect: Triggers enhanced review. User-token history scopes are unlikely to be approved without a concrete use case.
Common bot scope; still needs a written justification.

blockers.cause: Installing in a workspace other than the one that owns the app, before distribution is activated.
blockers.fix: Complete the Manage Distribution checklist and click Activate Public Distribution.

blockers.cause: Multiple redirect URLs are registered and the redirect_uri differs between the authorize and token calls, or it is not registered.
blockers.fix: Register the exact callback URL and send the same value in both calls.

blockers.cause: A scope does not exist or conflicts, or a published app requests scopes Slack has not approved.
blockers.fix: Correct the scope list; for published apps, get the scopes approved in review.

blockers.cause: Commercially distributed unlisted app created after May 29, 2025 that is not approved for the Marketplace.
blockers.fix: Get Marketplace approval, or build an internal customer app, which is not affected.
Reach 10 active workspaces and keep them throughout review.

blockers.cause: Disqualifying or unneeded scopes, an MCP-only app, LLM training on Slack data, or unexpected actions such as auto-joining channels.
blockers.fix: Trim scopes, add meaningful in-Slack functionality, and remove disallowed behavior.

composio.note: Managed auth is fine for connecting your own workspace or a private pilot. Its default scope list is broad and includes scopes that trigger enhanced Marketplace review (search:read.*, *:history, files:read). Use your own Slack app with trimmed scopes to distribute beyond a pilot or to list in the Marketplace. The conversations.history/replies limit applies to unlisted commercial apps whichever OAuth app is used. Composio's default redirect (https://backend.composio.dev/api/v1/auth-apps/add) would likely need to be registered as a Redirect URL on a custom app; this is inferred, not tested.

open_questions: Current Marketplace queue times: docs give ceilings only, with no published average.
Whether existing unlisted installs are now subject to the 1 req/min conversations.history limit; Slack's sources conflict.

Whether Composio's default redirect URL must be registered in a custom Slack app (inferred, untested).
The Submit to the App Directory checklist is behind login and was not viewed.
No documented install cap for unlisted apps was found.
The Composio default scopes were not checked one by one against Slack's scope reference.
Whether Enterprise Grid or org-wide deployment adds review steps was not verified.
